Explain in your own words what 'Biodegradation Bioplastics and Green Industry' refers to.
questions.a: Biodegradation recycles what refuse: plastic-eating bacteria, PHB bioplastic brewed by Alcaligenes eutrophus and stacked into Arabidopsis chloroplasts through three borrowed genes, biopulping fungi that spare energy in paper mills, xylanase biobleaching that trims chlorine, and oil-hungry engineered Pseudomonas superbugs for enhanced oil recovery and spill clean-up - biotechnology rewriting industry's environmental bill.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Biodegradation Bioplastics and Green Industry'.
questions.a: Swap petrochemistry for biology - biodegradable polymers, fungal pulping and oil-eating microbes shrink industry's footprint.

concepts.title: GM Crops for Resistance and Tolerance

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'GM Crops for Resistance and Tolerance' refers to.
questions.a: Transgenic crops fight on every front: Roundup Ready canola, soybean, corn and cotton overproduce a modified Agrobacterium enzyme to shrug off glyphosate; viral coat-protein genes vaccinate squash, potato and papaya against mosaic and ringspot viruses; antifungal defensins from alfalfa guard potatoes against Verticillium; lysozyme genes block Erwinia soft rot; Bt cotton remains India's only commercial transgenic since 2002 while Bangladesh pioneered Bt brinjal in 2014, and stacked pyramids pair insect resistance with drought tolerance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'GM Crops for Resistance and Tolerance'.
questions.a: Overproduce the target, vaccinate with a coat protein, or stack two traits - each strategy buys one specific resistance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'GM Crops for Resistance and Tolerance' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Regenerative Medicine and Organoids' refers to.
questions.a: Regenerative medicine replaces what degeneration destroys: autografts move tissue within one body, allografts between human donors and recipients, xenografts even borrow pig heart valves; stem cells coaxed in Matrigel hydrogel self-assemble into organoids - ultra-small three-dimensional tissues from pluripotent or adult stem cells - while spheroids, hanging drops, organs-on-chips and bioprinted scaffolds push Carticel cartilage repair, laViv fibroblast cosmetics and Dermagraft diabetic patches toward the clinic.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Regenerative Medicine and Organoids'.
questions.a: Seed stem cells into the right gel and geometry and they build the tissue for you - 3D culture is the body's own construction crew.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Regenerative Medicine and Organoids' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Nanobiotechnology and the Nano Scale' refers to.
questions.a: Shrink matter below a micron and it changes character: an atom spans 0.1 nanometres, a fullerene sixty carbons, DNA about two, with the scale running to a millimetre sand grain; gold that glitters yellow in bulk turns ruby red below thirty nanometres and pink up to a hundred while its surface area explodes with particle count, cadmium-selenide quantum dots fluoresce size-dependent colours, and carbon folds into fullerene, nanotube or graphene shapes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nanobiotechnology and the Nano Scale'.
questions.a: Size writes the properties - the same gold reads red at thirty nanometres and pink at a hundred.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Nanobiotechnology and the Nano Scale' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Nanomedicine Drug Delivery and EPR' refers to.
questions.a: Nanocarriers ferry drugs where they matter: liposomal amphotericin B tames the antifungal's toxicity, albumin-bound paclitaxel and liposomal doxorubicin ride the enhanced permeability and retention effect - twenty to thirty nanometre particles leaking through tumour vessels' fenestrations and staying trapped - while silver nanoparticles dress wounds, zinc and titanium oxides shield sunscreen skin, quantum-dot and lab-on-chip biosensors read biomarkers at the bedside.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Nanomedicine Drug Delivery and EPR'.
questions.a: Leaky tumour vessels admit only small nanocarriers, and the tumour's poor drainage keeps them there - that is targeted delivery.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Nanomedicine Drug Delivery and EPR' taught, and from which source text?
